title.narrative: Inledande kärnstöd till Kakheti Regional Development Foundation
Pre-Core support to Kakheti Regional Development Foundation

description.narrative:
Kakheti Regional Development Foundation, KRDF har inkommit med ett förslag om ett inledande kärnstöd (pre-core support) för att genomföra verksamhet inom organisationens strategi under perioden augusti 2019- januari 2020. Baserat på ambassadens dialog med KRDF är avsikten att bidraget kan utgöra en brygga till ett tentativt kärnstöd.
KRDF är en georgisk civilsamhällsorganisation som är grundad i, samt bedriver verksamhet i Kakheti och framför allt i Pankisi-dalen i östra Georgien. Pankisi-dalen bebos bland annat av olika etniska och religiösa minoritetsgrupper samt flyktingar från Tjetjenien. Regionen präglas av starkt konservativa värderingar, vilket innebär begränsade rättigheter för framför allt flickor och kvinnor. Isolering och fattigdom utgör även en grund för radikalisering, vilket förekommer och utgör en utmaning för unga män samt deras familjer i Pankisi-dalen.
KRDFs verksamhet utgår från en strategisk plan för perioden 2015-2019. Strategin specificerar fem huvudsakliga verksamhetsinriktningar, varav två utgör målsättningar för bryggstödet.
Ansökt budget uppgår efter avrundning till 300 000 SEK, vilken fördelas mellan två olika verksamhetsinriktningar samt personal och administrativa kostnader.
Under perioden när bryggstödet genomförs kommer ambassaden att via direktupphandling och avrop genomföra dels en granskning av intern styrning och kontroll samt stödja KRDF i processen att utvärdera och utveckla en ny strategi för perioden 2020 - 2024. Det är ambassadens avsikt att under hösten 2019 fortsätta dialogen med KRDF om ett tentativt kärnstöd för genomförande av den nya strategin.

Kakheti Regional Development Foundation, KRDF has applied for a pre-core support with the purpose to implement the organisation's strategy during August 2019 - January 2020. Based on the Embassy's dialgoue with KRDF the purpose is that the contribution will constitute a bridge towards a tentative core support.
KRDF is a Georgian civil society organisation which was founded in, and operate in the region of Kakheti and mainly in the Pankisi valley in the Eastern parts of Georgia. The Pankisi valley is inhabitated by different ethnic minorities and refugees from Chechneya and is an isolated region facing numerous challenges, including poverty and human rights. KRDF's operations are planned based on a strategic plan for the period 2015-2019. The strategy specifies five main directions of operations, out of which two will be the objectives for the pre-core support:
The budget applied for, after roundig is 300 000 SEK, which is divided between the different strategtic directions, staff and administrative costs.
During the period of implementation of the pre-core support the Embassy intends to, through direct procurement and a call-off from a framework agreement perform both a review of internal management and control, and support KRDF in the process to evaluate and develop a new strategy for 2020 - 2024. It is the Embassy's intention to during the autumn of 2019 continue the dialogue with KRDF about a tentative core support for the implementation of the new strategy.

Key strategic direction from KRDF’s Strategic plan for 2015-2019: Key strategic direction nr 1: Counselling and support of socially vulnerable persons, refugeees, IDP population and migrants and representation in administrative and judicial bodies. Key strategic direction nr 5: Civic education and integration of young people in Kakheti region.

The pre-core support has contributed to continued capacity building for youth and women in the Pankisi-valley. The majority of the participants in the implemented trainings have been women. Trainings have been offered within family medicine, handicraft, cultural activities and income generating trainings etc. According to the report three women have been able to to start their own business as a result of the trainings. Youth have been offered additional courses in Georgian and English language and mathematics as preparation for national exams. Gender equality and civic education are integrated into the different trainings. A joint winter camp for both Kist and Georgian youth combining civic education and leadership skills has been held. The camp has contributed to decrease prejudice and isolation between the different groups. KRDF's lawyer has provided legal support in 41 cases. The majority of the cases have been related to citizenship, right of residence and/or refugee status etc. Out of 29 cases in this area, 14 had a negative outcome, 7 had a positive outcome and 8 are still in process. The other 12 cases concern material legal disputes and family legal disputes. Out of these cases 5 had a negative outcome, 3 had a positive outcome and 4 are still in process. The pre-core support provided KRDF with an opportunity to initiate work in a new district of Kakheti, Karajala, a community to a large extent inhabited by another Georgian ethnic minority, Azeris, facing similar challenges as the Kist minority.
